_about: Plain-language labels for the oncologist report (scripts/build_report.py). Written by a senior heme-onc agent from rubric_v2.toml, case.toml and gold.json, then checked item by item against the rubric text by an independent heme-onc agent (2026-10-22). Not human-reviewed. Never shown to the model.

case_card.title: Stage III DLBCL with prior anthracycline and reduced LVEF
case_card.patient: 59F, breast cancer survivor (2016: dose-dense AC, cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast RT, on anastrozole), presents with left axillary mass, fevers to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats; ECOG 1, LDH 510. Non-GCB DLBCL (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, FISH negative for rearrangements), PET nodes above and below the diaphragm plus splenic nodules, marrow negative, and new LVEF 45% (62% in 2016) with GLS -14%.
tests: Spleen is a nodal site under Lugano, so stage is III, not IV, and IPI is 2.
Double-expressor by IHC but FISH-negative, so not double-hit; no intensification to DA-EPOCH-R.
Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean standard full-dose R-CHOP / Pola-R-CHP is not safe as is.
Treatment must stay curative: anthracycline-free (R-CEOP / R-GCVP) or cardio-protected regimen, with cardio-oncology input and cardioprotective drugs.
CNS-IPI 2 with no high-risk sites: no routine CNS prophylaxis.
case_card.correct_plan: Curative-intent R-CEOP x6 (R-GCVP as alternative) after urgent cardio-oncology review, with ACE inhibitor/ARB plus carvedilol replacing amlodipine and serial echo, troponin and NT-proBNP; R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane only if cardio-oncology judges it safe. No CNS prophylaxis, allopurinol and G-CSF support, and end-of-treatment PET-CT read with Deauville.

items.label: Diagnoses DLBCL, NOS, non-GCB phenotype by Hans algorithm
items.why: Correct histology and cell-of-origin subtype frame prognosis and every downstream treatment decision.

items.label: Notes Hans non-GCB is not molecular ABC by gene expression
items.why: Avoids overstating cell-of-origin; IHC surrogate may misclassify, which matters if ABC-targeted options are considered.

items.label: States axillary node is lymphoma, not breast cancer (keratin/GATA3 negative)
items.why: In a breast cancer survivor, excluding recurrence confirms one disease to treat, not two.

items.label: Stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III
items.why: Nodes on both sides of the diaphragm plus the spleen is stage III (the spleen counts as nodal tissue); the stage on record guides treatment and counselling.

items.label: Explains spleen is nodal tissue, so splenic nodules are not stage IV
items.why: Counting the spleen as an extranodal organ would wrongly upstage her to IV; marrow and other organs are uninvolved.

items.label: Notes B symptoms: fevers above 38 C and drenching night sweats
items.why: Documented fevers to 38.4 C and sweats define stage IIIB and reflect disease activity.

items.label: Notes 7.5 cm mass is below 10 cm Lugano bulk threshold
items.why: Bulk status affects risk and radiotherapy discussion; definitions vary, some trials use 7.5 cm.

items.label: Stages the disease as stage IV
items.why: Counting splenic nodules as extranodal overstages her. The IPI is unchanged (stage III and IV score the same), but the recorded stage and the counselling are wrong.

items.label: Calls it double-expressor (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%) but not double-hit
items.why: FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so standard-intensity curative therapy applies.

items.label: Classifies the lymphoma as double-hit with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements
items.why: FISH is negative; mislabelling as high-grade double-hit could drive unwarranted intensive, doxorubicin-containing therapy.

items.label: Recommends DA-EPOCH-R or intensified regimen for double-expressor biology
items.why: Double-expressor status alone does not justify intensification, and DA-EPOCH-R adds doxorubicin to a damaged heart.

items.label: Calculates IPI as 2 (low-intermediate risk)
items.why: Only elevated LDH and advanced stage (III-IV) score; age 59, ECOG 1 and no extranodal sites score zero.

items.label: Calculates CNS-IPI as 2 (intermediate risk)
items.why: Intermediate CNS risk underpins the decision not to give routine CNS prophylaxis.

items.label: States routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated
items.why: CNS-IPI 2 with no kidney, adrenal, testicular or breast involvement; avoids unnecessary toxicity.

items.label: Mandates CNS prophylaxis with high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal therapy
items.why: Not indicated at CNS-IPI 2 without high-risk sites; adds toxicity without proven benefit here.

items.label: Recognises anthracycline cardiac risk; avoids standard full-dose doxorubicin without addressing heart
items.why: Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean further full-dose doxorubicin risks heart failure.

items.label: Recommends standard R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP ignoring reduced LVEF
items.why: Unconditioned full-dose doxorubicin in established cardiac dysfunction risks irreversible heart failure.

items.label: Requests urgent cardio-oncology or cardiology evaluation before therapy
items.why: LVEF decline needs specialist assessment to choose a safe regimen and start cardioprotection before cycle 1.

items.label: Starts ACE inhibitor/ARB plus beta-blocker, e.g. replacing amlodipine
items.why: Guideline cardioprotection treats her cardiac dysfunction and controls her blood pressure during chemotherapy.

items.label: Recommends curative anthracycline-free or modified regimen, e.g. R-CEOP or R-GCVP
items.why: Keeps cure as the goal while sparing the heart; liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane only with cardio-oncology clearance.

items.label: Acknowledges anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy
items.why: She wants cure; the trade-off between cardiac safety and cure rate must be discussed honestly.

items.label: Plans serial LVEF/GLS imaging plus troponin and/or BNP monitoring
items.why: Detects further cardiac injury early during therapy in a patient with existing dysfunction.

items.label: Recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care or hospice
items.why: She is fit with curable disease; abandoning cure is wrong because the heart changes the regimen, not the goal.

items.label: Plans end-of-treatment PET-CT read with Lugano/Deauville criteria
items.why: Standard way to confirm complete metabolic response and decide on further management.

items.label: Assesses low-intermediate tumor lysis risk; gives allopurinol and hydration cycle 1
items.why: LDH about twice normal with a 7.5 cm mass; simple prevention avoids renal injury.

items.label: Recommends or considers primary G-CSF support with each cycle
items.why: Reduces febrile neutropenia and dose delays, preserving curative dose intensity.

items.label: Addresses ongoing anastrozole: continue, or hold with breast oncology
items.why: She asked directly; no meaningful interaction, but coordination with breast oncology is needed.

items.label: Confirms hepatitis B serology (HBsAg, anti-HBc) negative before rituximab
items.why: Excludes rituximab-related hepatitis B reactivation risk before starting therapy.

items.label: Judges her fit for curative therapy (ECOG 1); acknowledges goal of cure
items.why: Normal organ function apart from LVEF; her stated goal is cure and returning to work.

items.label: Lists cause of LVEF decline / cardio-oncology work-up as missing
items.why: Prior left chest RT raises coronary risk; ischemic evaluation, cardiac MRI, troponin and NT-proBNP define the cause.
